requirement_text: Only the candidates whose eligibility is defined in the “Principles Governing International Student Admissions” drawn up by the Council of Higher Education can apply to these quotas.
limitations: METU's page states no eligibility criteria of its own. A per-institution scrape of METU yields ZERO eligibility rules, which would read as 'no requirements' rather than 'defined elsewhere'.
researcher_notes: THE ANSWER TO THE MODELLING QUESTION. METU does NOT restate YÖK's eligibility rules - it REFERENCES them and links out to YÖK's own document. Sabancı, by contrast, restates the same rules in full on its own page. So Turkish universities fall into two patterns, restate-in-full and reference-only, over ONE shared national rule set. That settles it: the authoritative source is YÖK's 'Principles Governing International Student Admissions' itself, NOT any university page. Model the rule set once from YÖK and link institutions to it. Modelling per-institution would not merely duplicate - it would produce SIX DIFFERENT PARTIAL COPIES, because reference-only universities like METU never state the rules at all and would come out empty.

requirement_text: Students who meet the application criteria below may apply
limitations: Explicit negative: METU's own page carries no evaluable eligibility rule. The linked YÖK directive was NOT fetched by this lane and is the correct next target for whoever models the national rule set.
researcher_notes: The criteria themselves live in linked external documents (a scores PDF and a YÖK directive in Turkish), not on this page.

requirement_text: Reasoning Test: A minimum score of 1000 out of 1600 in “Math” and “Critical Reading” sections.
limitations: Verify current section naming against College Board before ingesting.
researcher_notes: The 1600 total is current, but 'Critical Reading' is retired College Board terminology - the current section is 'Evidence-based Reading and Writing' (the name Koç uses). A student reading this cannot tell which section of their score report to compare. Same defect class as the TOEFL scale problem: a threshold naming an instrument by a label the operator no longer issues.

requirement_text: Subject Test: A minimum score of 500 out of 800 from minimum two sections related to the applied program.
limitations: MUST be verified at College Board before ingestion. If the test is discontinued, the requirement is unsatisfiable and should never evaluate to not_met - a student cannot fail to take a test that no longer exists.
researcher_notes: FLAG, NOT A FINDING: SAT Subject Tests are believed to have been discontinued by College Board several years ago. That belief is this researcher's prior knowledge, which is a LEAD TO VERIFY and never evidence - so it is recorded as a flag against College Board, not asserted. If confirmed, this is a live published requirement citing an instrument no applicant can now sit, which is a third variant of the same family as the TOEFL and 'Critical Reading' cases.

requirement_text: A minimum diploma score of 28 out of 45. Mimimum one HL subject related to the applied program.
researcher_notes: IB. Verbatim including Bilkent's own typo ('Mimimum'). Notably lower than the UK institutions in this corpus (LSE 39, Imperial 41, Glasgow 36-38).

requirement_text: Minimum three A level subjects in particular area of the applied program with at least “C” grade.
Gold, Silver or Bronze Medal holders in International Science Olympiads recognized by TÜBİTAK
researcher_notes: An ACHIEVEMENT-based admission route, not a test-score route. Directly relevant to ORYN: a student's competition record can itself be an admission qualification here, not merely profile decoration.

requirement_text: Please note that applications with predicted grades/results/scores will not be evaluated.
researcher_notes: CONTRADICTS Koç University, which states 'You can apply with your predicted IB or A-level scores issued by your school.' This is NOT a conflict to flag - two universities may legitimately differ. It is recorded because it is decision-relevant in opposite directions for the same student in the same country: a student applying before final results can apply to Koç and CANNOT apply to Bilkent. Generic country-level advice would get one of them wrong.
